title: Can You Put Carpet in a Basement in Snohomish? Moisture Rules First
meta: Yes, carpet works in a Snohomish basement if the slab passes a moisture test and you choose synthetic fiber and pad. Wills Flooring explains the rules.
keywords: carpet in basement Snohomish, can you put carpet in a basement, basement carpet moisture, best carpet for basements WA, basement carpet pad moisture barrier

blocks.lead: Yes, you can carpet a Snohomish basement, but only after the slab passes a moisture test, and only with synthetic fiber and a moisture-resistant pad.
blocks.detail: Most basement carpet failures are not carpet problems, they are water problems nobody measured. Test first, then choose the carpet around what the test says. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft stretched in over pad or $1.29 glued straight to the slab, with carpet and pad quoted at the estimate.

blocks.html: Snohomish is a crawlspace town more than a basement town, but the daylight basements on Fobes Hill, the sloped lots around Blackmans Lake and the partial cellars downtown bring this question up every fall. Someone wants a warm media room below grade and wonders whether carpet is asking for trouble. Here is how we decide, in order.

blocks.text: Rule one: measure the moisture before you shop for carpet

items.text: Efflorescence on the walls, a tide line, rust at the base of the water heater, a musty smell after a week of rain. Any of these means a drainage fix comes before flooring.
items.note: Free at the estimate; we walk the whole basement.

items.text: A 2 ft square of plastic taped tight to the slab. If it fogs or the concrete darkens underneath, the slab is passing vapor and you need a barrier pad at minimum.
items.note: Cheap, and you can do it yourself before we visit.

items.text: For finished basements we prefer a relative humidity probe drilled into the slab. Pad and carpet makers generally want the slab under about 75 to 80 percent RH, and the room air under 60 percent.
items.note: This is the number that decides which pad you can use.

items.d: Check the walls and window wells
items.text: Snohomish acreage lots with clay soil hold water against foundations. Window wells without drains, and downspouts dumping at the foundation, are the two things we flag most.

items.title: Olefin (polypropylene)
items.text: Olefin does not absorb water, will not mildew from a damp slab, and is the fiber in most purpose-built basement carpets. It crushes faster than nylon in a hallway, but a basement family room is not a hallway. Loop and Berber styles hide the crushing.

items.title: Solution-dyed polyester or triexta
items.text: Both resist moisture and stains and feel softer underfoot than olefin. Triexta handles the wet-boots traffic Snohomish basements get from the back door. Choose solution-dyed so a cleaning mishap does not leave a bleach line.

items.title: Carpet tiles
items.text: Modular tiles with a hard vinyl or fiberglass back are the safest option when the slab tests borderline. If a corner gets wet you lift a dozen tiles, dry the slab and put them back. The look is more office than living room.

items.title: Skip these
items.text: Wool, jute-backed carpet, anything with a natural fiber backing, and thick high-pile cut piles. Wool holds water and feeds mildew, jute rots, and dense pile dries slowly. All are wonderful upstairs and wrong down here.

blocks.text: The pad matters more than the carpet

head: Pad type
Below-grade verdict
Why
rows: Standard rebond is a sponge. A vapor-barrier film on top keeps slab moisture out of the backing, but the pad still holds water if the slab weeps.
Dense, flat, absorbs little water and dries fast. Firmer feel, which most people accept in a basement.
Closed-cell rubber barely absorbs water and feels solid. Costs more, and the slab must be flat because rubber shows every bump.
Comfortable upstairs. Below grade it acts like a reservoir and takes days to dry once wet.
Good for tiles and commercial loop
Nothing to hold water, easy to dry, fastest to reinstall after a leak. This is the $1.29 glue-down rate, and it is what we use on borderline slabs.
blocks.note: Stretch-in over a barrier pad is $0.99 per sq ft in labor, glue-down straight to the slab $1.29, both with a 500 sq ft minimum. Carpet and pad are quoted once we have the slab reading.

blocks.text: When carpet is the wrong answer for the basement

a.title: Go ahead when
items: The 72-hour tape test stays dry and the RH probe is in range
No history of standing water, ever
The basement is heated like the rest of the house
Olefin, triexta or solution-dyed polyester over a barrier pad

b.title: Stop when
items: The slab has flooded once, even years ago
Efflorescence or a tide line on the walls
The space is unheated, or the yard door is the main entry
You want wool, thick plush or a natural-backed carpet

blocks.html: When we tell a Snohomish homeowner no on carpet, the usual replacement is a rigid-core vinyl plank over the slab with a large area rug on top: warm where you sit, waterproof everywhere else. Compare the labor first. A 700 sq ft daylight basement is 700 x $1.29 = $903 in glue-down carpet labor against 700 x $2.50 = $1,750 for plank, both plus material.

blocks.title: One Snohomish-specific warning:
blocks.text: Wood and pellet stoves are common in local basements and they dry the room air in winter, which hides a wet slab. A basement that smells fine in January can be at 70 percent RH by April. Test in the wet months.
Two real Snohomish basements, two different answers

items.title: Carpet approved
items.text: The slab probe came in under the limit, downspouts already ran to daylight and the room had a heat register. They chose a solution-dyed triexta loop over a film-faced rebond, with a dehumidifier on a drain line. Two winters in, no odor and no seam cupping.

items.title: Carpet declined
items.text: The tape test fogged in a day and a tide line ran eight inches up the block wall. We recommended a sump and perimeter drain first, then glue-down carpet tile or vinyl plank. A pad on that floor would have come out within a year.

blocks.text: How to get a basement carpet that lasts

items.html: Ask for the slab reading in writing. Any installer willing to carpet a basement without measuring is guessing with your money.
Run a dehumidifier from day one. Below 60 percent room RH, mildew never gets started. Put it on a hose to a drain so you never have to empty it.
Pick the pad for the slab, not for the feel. A firmer synthetic or rubber pad is the difference between a ten-year floor and a three-year one.
Keep the seams away from the wettest wall. Seam placement is free to plan and expensive to fix. Tell us where the sump, the door and the window wells are.

Get the pad, fiber and moisture barrier named on the quote. Ours lists all three next to the labor rate, so you can compare it honestly against anyone else's. See the carpet installation page for what is included.

faq.q: Can you put carpet directly on a concrete basement floor?
faq.a: Physically yes, but not without a moisture test first. Direct glue-down, which we bill at $1.29 per sq ft, works well for carpet tiles and commercial loop when the slab is dry. For a family room, stretch-in carpet over a moisture-barrier pad at $0.99 per sq ft is more comfortable underfoot.

faq.q: What is the best carpet for a basement in Washington?
faq.a: Olefin or solution-dyed triexta in a loop or low cut pile, over a synthetic, rubber or film-faced pad. Those fibers do not absorb water and dry fast. In the Snohomish area the wet season is long, so we also recommend a dehumidifier plumbed to a drain.

faq.q: Does carpet in a basement cause mold?
faq.a: Carpet does not cause mold. Trapped moisture with no way to dry does. Wool or jute-backed carpet on a weeping slab with a foam pad will grow mildew. Synthetic carpet on a tested slab, over a barrier pad, with room humidity under 60 percent, will not.

faq.q: How do I know if my basement slab is too wet for carpet?
faq.a: Tape a two-foot square of plastic to the slab for 72 hours. If the concrete underneath darkens or the plastic fogs, moisture is coming through. We follow up with an in-slab relative humidity probe at the estimate, which gives a number the pad manufacturer can accept or reject.

faq.q: Should I put a vapor barrier under basement carpet?
faq.a: Yes, in some form. The simplest is a pad with a vapor-barrier film face. For damp slabs a closed-cell rubber pad does the same job with less risk. A loose plastic sheet under regular pad is not recommended, because it traps water on top of itself and wrinkles under the carpet.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank better than carpet for a Snohomish basement?
faq.a: For a basement with any moisture history, yes. Rigid-core vinyl plank does not care about a damp slab, and an area rug gives you softness where you sit. On price, carpet labor is $0.99 per sq ft stretched in or $1.29 glued down and plank is $2.50, so carpet is cheaper to install but riskier below grade.
